reason: The run is already consistent across all 102 verses. In Jesus' introductory formula ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν/σοι it is always "truly" ("Truly I tell you"), and John's doubled ἀμὴν ἀμήν is always "Truly, truly". As a liturgical response, a doxology or prayer closing, and the title in Revelation 3:14, it is always transliterated "Amen". These are two distinct uses, each rendered in the standard modern way, so the difference between "truly" and "Amen" is a sense difference, not inconsistency. The only variation is punctuation in John ("Truly, truly I tell you" versus "Truly, truly, I tell you") and capitalisation or exclamation marks on "Amen", which are style matters rather than lexical choices.
